title: streaming-token-reassembly-resilience-and-adaptive-backpressure-plan
creator: Mariana Cole
description:
Summary:
During a capacity surge on 2026-02-27 we observed a class of streaming failures where client connections terminated with only partial token fragments delivered, followed by session-level disconnects and opaque retries. Root cause analysis showed three contributing factors: 1) aggressive upstack client backpressure combined with server-side batching heuristics led to premature connection resets; 2) token fragment reassembly logic in the streaming dispatcher did not tolerate reordered chunk acknowledgements under pause/resume; 3) limited session-level telemetry made it hard to distinguish network flaps from server-side throttling.

This ticket defines the resilience plan: improve fragment reassembly, introduce durable resume tokens, add per-session backpressure telemetry, and implement an adaptive throttler that ties token-emission rate to live queue lengths and KV-cache warmness. Work items include instrumentation, small runtime changes, API compatibility tests, a canary rollout, and alert/runbook updates.

Why this matters:
- Customers experience incomplete responses and inconsistent retry behavior, affecting UX and perceived model quality.
- Incidents require manual investigation; better telemetry + automatic mitigation reduces MTTR and user-visible failures.

Scope:
- Streaming dispatcher: robust fragment buffer with checksums and sequence guards.
- Resume token: durable, compact token that includes session seq, KV cache snapshot id, and server-side slot hint.
- Adaptive throttler: runtime policy that reduces batch size and switches to low-latency path when session lag > threshold.
- Telemetry: new per-session metrics (emit_rate, queue_depth, fragment_reassembly_errors), traces with end-to-end trace_id for each stream.
- Console: dashboard panels and thresholds, and a runbook for the operator to triage reassembly vs network faults.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting the entire streaming protocol. We focus on incremental, backward-compatible changes and safe defaults for older clients.

Links:
- Incident timeline and timeline artifacts: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-02-27-streaming-fragments
- Postmortem doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Partial+Token+Fragments+Postmortem
- Initial RCA notes (internal): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XhRy-example
- Planned design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Streaming+Reassembly+Design

activity: 2026-03-01 - Mariana Cole created ticket and linked incident artifacts.
2026-03-02 - Eng sync: agreed scope and prioritized telemetry first; Arjun assigned as owner.

2026-03-04 - Spike complete: prototype fragment buffer with checksum and seq guards (branch: streaming/reassembly-spike). Performance microbenchmarks show +2ms median latency at 99th after reassembly enabled.
2026-03-06 - Design review with runtime and SDK teams. Feedback: resume token must be compact (<=256 bytes) and opt-in for older clients. Action: add compatibility header versioning.
2026-03-08 - Implemented per-session metrics: stream.emit_rate, stream.queue_depth, stream.fragment_errors. Dashboards in Datadog: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/streaming-reassembly (staging).
2026-03-09 - Added unit tests for out-of-order chunk delivery and simulated client pause/resume scenarios. 23 new tests added to streaming_reassembly_test.go.
2026-03-10 - Security review flagged resume token composition for secrets; decision: include only derived snapshot ids and slot hints, no raw KVs. Open follow-up: ENG-41209 (KMS review).

2026-03-11 - Canary rollout plan approved by SRE: 5% traffic for runtime-1.22 with reassembly enabled, monitoring rules and automated rollback on 3 consecutive increase in fragment_errors across canary hosts.
2026-03-12 - Began implementing adaptive throttler; prototype integrates queue_depth and kv_warmness. Benchmarking scheduled for 2026-03-14.
acceptance_criteria: Fragment reassembly handles out-of-order and partial chunks with checksum verification and no data duplication observed in 1M synthetic streams.
Resume tokens issued to new clients are backward-compatible; older clients continue to receive stream data unchanged.
Per-session telemetry emits metrics with cardinality controls and is visible in Console dashboards with alert thresholds.
Canary at 5% shows no increase in 5xx streaming errors or fragment_errors for 48h; SLO degradation < 0.2%.
Runbook updated and on-call knows rollback steps and how to interpret new metrics.
